title: Coding (JavaScript, graded by unit tests in a sandbox)

items.prompt: Write a JavaScript function isPalindrome(s) that returns true if the string s reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and any character that is not a letter or digit.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

items.prompt: Write a JavaScript function sumEven(numbers) that returns the sum of the even integers in the array numbers (0 for an empty array).

Write a JavaScript function fizzBuzz(n) that returns an array of strings for 1..n: "FizzBuzz" for multiples of 15, "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5, otherwise the number as a string.

Write a JavaScript function formatNaira(amount) that formats a non-negative number as Nigerian naira with the ₦ sign, comma thousands separators and exactly two decimal places. Examples: formatNaira(1234567.5) returns "₦1,234,567.50"; formatNaira(0) returns "₦0.00".

Write a JavaScript function isNigerianMobile(s) that returns true only for these two formats: (1) "0" followed by 7, 8 or 9, then 0 or 1, then exactly 8 more digits (11 digits in total, e.g. "08031234567"); (2) "+234" followed by 7, 8 or 9, then 0 or 1, then exactly 8 more digits (e.g. "+2348031234567"). No spaces or other characters are allowed.

Write a JavaScript function wordCount(text) that returns an object mapping each word (lower-cased) to how many times it appears. Words are runs of the letters a–z (after lower-casing); everything else separates words.
Write a JavaScript function fib(n) that returns the nth Fibonacci number, with fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1. It must be fast for n up to 70.
Write a JavaScript function chunk(array, size) that splits the array into consecutive groups of length size (the last group may be shorter).
Write a JavaScript function flatten(value) that flattens arbitrarily nested arrays into a single flat array, keeping the order.
Write a JavaScript function romanToInt(s) that converts a valid Roman numeral string (I, V, X, L, C, D, M, including subtractive forms like IV and CM) to an integer.
Write a JavaScript function gcd(a, b) that returns the greatest common divisor of two non-negative integers (gcd(0, 0) is 0).
